We have \(a = AB\), \(c = CD\) with \(a+c=12\); \(b = BC\), \(d = AD\) with \(b+d=13\). For orthogonal diagonals, \(a^2+c^2 = b^2+d^2\). Ptolemy gives area \(= \frac12(ac+bd)\). Maximize \(S = ac+bd\).
\[
a^2+c^2 = (a+c)^2-2ac = 144-2ac,\quad b^2+d^2 = 169-2bd
\]
\[
144-2ac = 169-2bd \implies bd - ac = \frac{25}{2}
\]
So \(S = 2ac + \frac{25}{2}\). To maximize \(S\), maximize \(ac\).
Reality of \(b,d\): \((b+d)^2 \ge 4bd \implies 169 \ge 4(ac+\frac{25}{2}) \implies ac \le \frac{119}{4}\).
Equality when \(b=d=\frac{13}{2}\). Then \(a,c\) from \(a+c=12\), \(ac=\frac{119}{4}\) (real and positive). Hence max \(S = 72\) and max area \(=36\).

\boxed{36}
